key_insight: UniMem combines episodic memory with parametric memory so LLM agents can both quickly learn from new tasks and gradually turn recurring behaviors into fast, stable internal skills. This helps them adapt to evolving task streams without relying only on slow retrieval at inference time.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the stability-plasticity dilemma in boundary-agnostic task streams: external retrieval memory can absorb new experiences but may not internalize reusable patterns, while parametric memory is efficient once learned but is harder to update without forgetting.
method: Uses complementary episodic-to-parametric memory to capture task experience and transfer repeated execution patterns into model parameters.
Supports boundary-agnostic, evolving streams where task changes are not clearly segmented, reducing dependence on explicit task boundaries.
Aims to preserve adaptability to new evidence while improving efficiency and stability for recurring tasks.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, UniMem offers a path toward agents that learn continuously in realistic environments without expensive retrieval overhead on every step. It is especially relevant for long-running assistants and tool-using systems that must balance fast adaptation with reliable reuse of prior skills.

paper_title: UniMem: Complementary Episodic-to-Parametric Memory for Boundary-Agnostic Task Streams
paper_authors: Siyu Xia, Chenheng Zhang, Yanting Wu, Haoxuan Li, Jiajun Chai
